t: 3723. Maximize Sum of Squares of Digits
o: Among all `num`-digit numbers with digit sum `sum`, maximize Σd² (ties broken by larger number). Since x² is convex, concentrating mass into 9s is optimal: as many leading 9s as possible, then one leftover digit, then trailing zeros. This simultaneously yields the lexicographically largest number, satisfying the tie-break. Impossible when the required digits exceed `num` (sum > 9·num). With num up to 2·10⁵ we must build a string, never an integer.
k: Convexity of x² means fewer, larger digits beat spreading the sum.

a.i: Place ⌊sum/9⌋ nines first, then the remainder digit (if nonzero), then pad with zeros to reach exactly `num` digits. Any other distribution can be improved by moving a unit from a smaller digit to a larger one (exchange argument).
a.t: O(num) — building the result string dominates

w: Only one meaningful approach exists; justify optimality with an exchange argument (merging two digits into a bigger one never decreases the square-sum). Pitfalls: off-by-one on padding when rem = 0, and forgetting the impossibility check. Follow-up: minimize the score instead (spread digits as evenly as possible).
